I am a 44-year-old woman farming 1.26 hectares of rented land here in the North East. Because this plot is rented and I have to pay the landowner, I cannot afford to buy chemical fertilizer from the agro-dealer this season, and I do not have enough livestock manure to cover this whole field. I will plant bean seeds I saved from last year’s harvest, but I must buy some insecticide because the pod borers and aphids always attack our cowpea if we do not spray at least once or twice. My children and I will do most of the clearing, planting, weeding, and harvesting by hand, though I will likely hire a few day laborers to help with the heavy weeding work when the rains start.
